chunks: Common resistor packages and sizes. The question: What are some common resistor packages and sizes?
Surface-mount (SMD) resistors come in standard sizes. Each size has a four-digit code that gives its length and width.
A bigger resistor can shed more heat, so it can handle more power and a higher voltage. A smaller one takes less board space but handles less power.
Think of pots and pans on a stove. A large pan has more surface to spread and shed heat, so it copes with a bigger flame. A tiny pan on a big flame scorches fast.
Resistors are the same: the larger body can dissipate more power before it overheats.
The analogy leaves out voltage, which also limits small parts because the gap between their ends is short.
Body sizes grow from 0402 to 2512; the darker ends are the metal terminations.
Larger bodies carry heat to bigger pads, which is what raises the power rating (a 2512 has about 40 times the body area of a 0402 and roughly 10 to 20 times the typical power rating).
SMD: surface-mount device, a part soldered flat onto the board surface. Package code (0603): the size in hundredths of an inch, so 0603 is 0. 06 by 0. 03 inch, about 1. 6 by 0.
8 mm. Power rating: the most heat the part can dissipate continuously. Derating: using the part well below its rating, often at half, for a safety margin.
Through-hole: a part with leads that go through holes in the board.
Put 5 volts across a 100 ohms resistor. The power is V squared over R equals 25 over 100 equals 0. 25 watts. Derate by half and you want a part rated for at least 0. 5 watts.
A 0603 is about 0. 1 watts, and a 1206 is about 0. 25 watts, so both are too small. A 2512 at about 1 watts works. That is the whole idea.
"SMD resistors are named in hundredths of an inch: 0402 is about 1 by 0. 5 millimeters, 0603 is 1. 6 by 0. 8, 0805, 1206, and up to 2512 for around a watt.
Power rating scales with size, roughly 1/16 to 1/10 watt for 0402 and 0603, 1/4 watt for 1206, 1 watt for 2512, and voltage rating scales too.
Through-hole is mostly 1/4 watt axial, plus wirewound and chassis types for power. I'd pick by derated power, voltage, and how it'll be assembled."
